Theme

Household, washing & chores · Computing & programming

charge verb

a battery, a phone

also recharge, charge up, fully charged, flat, dead battery, run out of battery

* our formation

Cic. Prov. Cons. 2.4: exhaustās domōs (sc. replēre; Lewis & Short)

* (our own formation) repleō, replēre, replēvī, replētum

verb, second conjugation; the full phrase is vī ēlectricā replēre

fill up again: charge, recharge

Our choice: no reference work gives a Latin verb for charging a battery. Classically replēre is to fill again what has been emptied, and Cicero pairs it with exhaustus, which gives the rest of the vocabulary: exhaustus, flat or dead; plēnus, fully charged. The meaning is plain at first hearing.

Other words

  • * (our own formation) compleō, complēre, complēvī, complētum — fill up: charge fully

    verb, second conjugation · also used · * our formation · Lewis & Short s.v. compleo: “to fill up, fill full” (class.)

  • * (our own formation) onerō, onerāre, onerāvī, onerātum — load

    verb, first conjugation · also used · * our formation

    The figure the modern languages use (French charger, Italian caricare, German laden), so it will be understood; but in Latin it suggests a burden laid on something, not a store filled up.

Examples

  • Accumulātrum paene exhaustum est; tēlephōnum replē.

    The battery’s nearly flat; charge your phone.composed

  • Jam plēnum est.

    It’s fully charged now.composed

See also battery, charger, plug in, socket.

SourcesLewis & Short: repleo · Lewis & Short: compleo · Lewis & Short: onero · Lewis & Short: exhaurio
